verdict: AMD crosses $1T on AI accelerator momentum; MRVL +6% on 2nm optical at ECOC; solar names +5-6%+ on tariff news; DRAM pricing moderating but still rising; HBM sold-out through 2027 — broad bull tone across AI/semi/solar complex.
body_md:
## Fresh Developments (Sep 21–24, 2026)

**AMD crosses $1T market cap (Sep 21)** — AMD surged ~9.6% in a single session, joining Nvidia, Broadcom, and Micron in the $1T club after a five-day +25% run (+180% YTD). Catalyst: data center revenue more than doubling YoY; MI400/Helios rack-scale system confirmed on track for 2H-2026 launch.

**MRVL +6.1% on 2nm optical debut at ECOC 2026 (Sep 22–23)** — Marvell showcased industry-first 2nm optical interconnects in Málaga, including a 102.4 Tbps co-packaged optics platform, 1.6T ZR+, and 400G-per-lane PAM4. Morgan Stanley raised its price target to $268 ahead of the Oct 6 Investor Day. Stock reached ~$262.

**COHR PhotonLink platform launch (Sep 20–21, ECOC)** — Coherent unveiled its PhotonLink integrated optics platform, integrating InP lasers, VCSEL arrays, silicon photonics, specialty fibers, and detectors. CPO and NPO production ramping 2026–2027; chip-to-chip by 2030. Presented live at ECOC alongside a 25.6 Tbps line system demo.

**Solar names +5–6%+ on polysilicon tariff report** — The Trump administration is reportedly preparing 25–50% tariffs and a minimum price floor on imported polysilicon and solar cells/modules, targeting Chinese supply chains. FSLR, ENPH, and ARRY each gained 5–6%+.

**TrendForce 3Q26 DRAM print** — Server DRAM contract prices +13–18% QoQ in 3Q26, a deliberate deceleration from Q1's +93–98% surge. Spot HBM3E (36 GB module) still trades at ~$2,100 vs. $300–$400 LTA pricing — extreme spread intact. HBM negotiations remain in flux but upside is retained.

**Micron Q4 FY26 earnings due Sep 30** — Guidance: $50B revenue (±$1B), $31 non-GAAP EPS (±$1). HBM3E/HBM4 fully booked through 2027, demand extending to 2028. $22B in strategic customer agreements secured in Q3. Free cash flow expected to exceed $30B in Q4.

**SK Hynix HBM4 ramp slipped to Q3** — Delayed from Q2 due to sustained HBM3E demand; HBM3E sites kept running longer. Samsung targeting 250K wafers/month HBM by end-2026 (+47% from 170K). No fresh correction-phase confirmation — baseline risk signal unchanged.

**HIVE/BUZZ** — No material fresh news in the last 24–72h. Most recent known catalyst: $220M GPU cloud contract (Bell Canada/Cohere, June 2026) and ProCogia sovereign AI partnership (earlier in September).

## Context vs Baseline

- **DRAM moderating** but positive. Baseline called for elevated pricing; Q3's +13–18% is expected deceleration, not a collapse.
- **HBM sold-out thesis intact**: SK Hynix HBM3E demand delaying HBM4; Micron $50B Q4 guide with orders to 2028 confirms. The key baseline risk — correction after 2026 — has not materialized yet; watch late-2026 capacity additions by all three suppliers.
- **Hyperscaler capex** at $725B collective now exceeds the $600–700B baseline — no guide-down detected.
- **AMD $1T** firmly validates the custom-silicon share-shift thesis (Signal 4). Not displacing NVDA, but the AI-accelerator duopoly is real.
- **Optical** accelerating: MRVL (2nm CPO) and COHR (PhotonLink) both live at ECOC with next-gen roadmaps. CPO entering production-ramp phase consistent with baseline CPO scale-out first view.
- **Solar**: US polysilicon tariffs are structurally bullish for FSLR (cadmium telluride, not polysilicon-dependent) and domestically positioned ENPH.

## Most Important Development

**AMD crossing $1T market cap on Sep 21 (+9.6% in one session) is the single most stock-moving event of the window.** Paired with MRVL +6% on industry-first 2nm optical at ECOC, both events validate the AI accelerator + optical infrastructure super-cycle thesis. The near-term event to watch: **Micron Q4 FY26 earnings on Sep 30** ($50B guided, HBM booked to 2028) — beats could re-rate MU and the memory complex; guidance on HBM4 pricing signals the first real datapoint on the post-2026 correction risk.
